description:
## Goal Implement `Filament.LiveComponent` — a Phoenix.LiveComponent that manages a Filament fiber tree, allowing Filament components to be embedded inside a regular Phoenix LiveView that uses `assigns` normally. This is the "Filament inside LiveView" direction only. The reverse (a Filament fiber hosting a Phoenix.LiveComponent) is Phase 2 and is NOT part of this ticket. After this ticket, users can write: ```heex <.live_component module={Filament.LiveComponent} id="my-cart" component={CartView} server={@cart_server} /> ``` inside any existing Phoenix LiveView template, without `use Filament.LiveView`. ## Deviation policy Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run `bw comment "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance. Do not improvise. --- ## 0. Prerequisites — read implementations first Before writing any code, read: - `lib/filament/live_view.ex` — Filament.LiveView macro (the existing full-LiveView adapter) This is the reference implementation. Filament.LiveComponent does the same thing but as a Phoenix.LiveComponent lifecycle (mount/1, update/2, handle_event/3) instead of a Phoenix.LiveView lifecycle (mount/3, render/1, handle_event/3, handle_info/3). - `lib/filament/reconciler.ex` — Reconciler.mount and Reconciler.update signatures - `lib/filament/fiber_tree.ex` — FiberTree.get_event_handler/3 - Phoenix.LiveComponent documentation: https://hexdocs.pm/phoenix_live_view/Phoenix.LiveComponent.html Key facts about LiveComponent: (a) Runs in the PARENT LiveView process — no separate process, no handle_info/3 (b) update/2 is called on mount AND on every parent re-render where props change (c) handle_event/3 receives events from the component's template (d) Messages to the component arrive at the parent LiveView's handle_info/3; the parent must call `Phoenix.LiveView.send_update/3` to push them to the component --- ## 1. Architecture ### How it works `Filament.LiveComponent` is a Phoenix.LiveComponent that manages a Filament fiber tree: - `mount/1` — called once. Store initial fiber state in socket assigns. - `update/2` — called on mount AND whenever parent LiveView re-renders with new assigns. Extract the `component:` and other assigns → call Reconciler.mount or Reconciler.update. - `handle_event/3` — dispatch `filament:` events to the registered event handler. - `render/1` — return the Filament rendered output. Observable updates (`:filament_observable_update`, `:filament_set_state`, etc.) arrive at the PARENT LiveView's handle_info/3, NOT directly to the LiveComponent. The parent must forward them to the LiveComponent via `send_update/3`. ### Propagating observable updates (user responsibility for Phase 1) For Phase 1, document that users must add the following to their parent LiveView if the embedded Filament component uses `use_observable` or `use_state`: ```elixir def handle_info({msg_type, _fiber_id, _slot, _val} = msg, socket) when msg_type in [ :filament_set_state, :filament_observable_update, :filament_observable_resubscribe ] do Phoenix.LiveView.send_update(Filament.LiveComponent, id: "my-cart", filament_msg: msg) {:noreply, socket} end ``` And `Filament.LiveComponent.update/2` handles the `filament_msg:` assign specially. This is a known limitation of Phoenix.LiveComponent's architecture. Document it clearly. --- ## 2. Implementation FILE: `lib/filament/live_component.ex` ```elixir defmodule Filament.LiveComponent do @moduledoc """ Phoenix LiveComponent adapter for embedding a Filament component inside a regular Phoenix LiveView. ## Usage <.live_component module={Filament.LiveComponent} id="unique-id" component={MyApp.MyComponent} my_prop="value" other_prop={@something} /> All assigns other than `id` and `component` are passed as props to the Filament component. ## Observable updates Because `Filament.LiveComponent` runs inside the parent LiveView process, observable update messages (`:filament_set_state`, `:filament_observable_update`) arrive at the parent's `handle_info/3`. The parent must forward them: def handle_info({type, _fid, _slot, _val} = msg, socket) when type in [:filament_set_state, :filament_observable_update, :filament_observable_resubscribe] do Phoenix.LiveView.send_update(Filament.LiveComponent, id: "my-id", filament_msg: msg) {:noreply, socket} end This is a Phase 1 limitation. Phase 2 will add automatic forwarding. """ use Phoenix.LiveComponent alias Filament.Reconciler # Called once before update/2. Initialise fiber_tree as nil to signal first mount. @impl true def mount(socket) do {:ok, assign(socket, :_filament_tree, nil)} end @impl true def update(%{filament_msg: msg} = _assigns, socket) do # Forward a Filament internal message from the parent LiveView. # Process it against the current fiber tree and re-render. tree = socket.assigns._filament_tree case process_filament_msg(msg, tree, self()) do {:ok, new_tree, new_rendered} -> {:ok, socket |> assign(:_filament_tree, new_tree) |> assign(:_filament_rendered, new_rendered)} :ignore -> {:ok, socket} end end def update(assigns, socket) do component = Map.fetch!(assigns, :component) # All assigns except :id, :component, :filament_msg are props excluded = [:id, :component, :filament_msg] props = assigns |> Map.drop(excluded) |> Map.new() case socket.assigns._filament_tree do nil -> # First mount — initialise fiber tree {tree, rendered, _pending_effects} = Reconciler.mount(component, props, owner_pid: self()) {:ok, socket |> assign(:_filament_tree, tree) |> assign(:_filament_rendered, rendered) |> assign(:_filament_component, component)} tree -> # Props changed — reconcile root_fiber_id = "root" {new_tree, rendered, _pending_effects} = Reconciler.update(tree, root_fiber_id, props, owner_pid: self()) {:ok, socket |> assign(:_filament_tree, new_tree) |> assign(:_filament_rendered, rendered)} end end @impl true def handle_event("filament:" <> ref, params, socket) do case String.split(ref, ":", parts: 2) do [fiber_id_str, index_str] -> handler_index = String.to_integer(index_str) tree = socket.assigns._filament_tree handler = Filament.FiberTree.get_event_handler(tree, fiber_id_str, handler_index) case handler do nil -> {:noreply, socket} fun when is_function(fun, 0) -> fun.(); {:noreply, socket} fun when is_function(fun, 1) -> fun.(params); {:noreply, socket} _other -> {:noreply, socket} end _ -> {:noreply, socket} end end @impl true def render(assigns) do assigns._filament_rendered end # ── Private ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── defp process_filament_msg({:filament_set_state, fiber_id, slot_index, new_value}, tree, owner_pid) do case Map.get(tree, fiber_id) do nil -> :ignore fiber -> new_slots = Map.put(fiber.hook_slots, slot_index, new_value) new_tree = Map.put(tree, fiber_id, %{fiber | hook_slots: new_slots}) {new_tree, rendered, _effects} = Reconciler.update(new_tree, fiber_id, fiber.props, owner_pid: owner_pid) {:ok, new_tree, rendered} end end defp process_filament_msg({:filament_observable_update, fiber_id, slot_index, new_value}, tree, owner_pid) do case Map.get(tree, fiber_id) do nil -> :ignore fiber -> existing = Map.get(fiber.hook_slots, slot_index, :uninitialized) server = case existing do {:subscribed, s, _v} -> s _ -> nil end new_slots = Map.put(fiber.hook_slots, slot_index, {:subscribed, server, new_value}) new_tree = Map.put(tree, fiber_id, %{fiber | hook_slots: new_slots}) {new_tree, rendered, _effects} = Reconciler.update(new_tree, fiber_id, fiber.props, owner_pid: owner_pid) {:ok, new_tree, rendered} end end defp process_filament_msg({:filament_observable_resubscribe, fiber_id, slot_index}, tree, owner_pid) do case Map.get(tree, fiber_id) do nil -> :ignore fiber -> new_slots = Map.put(fiber.hook_slots, slot_index, :needs_resubscribe) new_tree = Map.put(tree, fiber_id, %{fiber | hook_slots: new_slots}) {new_tree, rendered, _effects} = Reconciler.update(new_tree, fiber_id, fiber.props, owner_pid: owner_pid) {:ok, new_tree, rendered} end end defp process_filament_msg(_unknown, _tree, _owner_pid), do: :ignore end ``` NOTES ON IMPLEMENTATION: - `Reconciler.mount/3` and `Reconciler.update/4` — check actual signatures in `lib/filament/reconciler.ex`. Adapt the calls above to match exactly. The third argument to mount/3 is a keyword list with `:owner_pid`. The fourth argument to update/4 is the same. - `pending_effects` returned by Reconciler — in Filament.LiveView, effects are processed via `attach_hook(:after_render, ...)`. In a LiveComponent, attach_hook is available on the socket. Use the same approach: `Phoenix.LiveView.attach_hook(socket, :filament_effects, :after_render, &Filament.LiveView.run_pending_effects/1)` Add this to the mount/1 implementation. OR: store pending_effects in socket assigns and process them in update/2 before returning. Whichever approach matches what Filament.LiveView already does. - The `owner_pid: self()` — in a LiveComponent, `self()` is the PARENT LiveView pid. This is correct: observable update messages should go to the parent LiveView process (they can't go directly to the component since it has no process of its own). If these notes reveal a fundamental incompatibility (e.g., Reconciler API is very different), stop and comment on the ticket. --- ## 3. Tests FILE: `test/filament/live_component_test.exs` ```elixir defmodule Filament.LiveComponentTest do use ExUnit.Case, async: true # Define a minimal Filament component for testing defmodule TestComp do use Filament.Component defcomponent TestComp do prop :label, :string, default: "default" def render(assigns) do {count, set_count} = use_state(0) ~F"""
{@label} {count}
""" end end end test "mount renders initial props" do # Test that update/2 on a fresh socket (tree=nil) mounts correctly {:ok, socket} = Filament.LiveComponent.mount(%Phoenix.LiveView.Socket{ assigns: %{__changed__: %{}, __given__: %{}} }) assigns = %{id: "test1", component: TestComp, label: "Hello"} {:ok, updated_socket} = Filament.LiveComponent.update(assigns, socket) rendered = updated_socket.assigns._filament_rendered assert rendered != nil html = Filament.Test.rendered_to_string(rendered) assert html =~ "Hello" assert html =~ "0" end test "handle_event dispatches to filament event handler" do # ... mount, get the rendered HTML, find the filament: ref, dispatch it # Assert the state update triggers a re-render with count=1 # This test is more involved — adapt based on actual rendered output end end ``` NOTE: These tests exercise the LiveComponent lifecycle without a real Phoenix socket. Check whether `Phoenix.LiveView.Socket` can be constructed directly in tests or whether a different approach is needed. If direct socket construction is not practical, use the Rung 4 test approach (Phoenix.LiveViewTest with a host LiveView) instead. If that is also not practical in this context, document the gap and add a future ticket. The priority is that `Filament.LiveComponent` compiles, its callbacks are correct, and the logic is sound. Exhaustive testing via the component lifecycle is deferred to a future integration test if socket construction is difficult. --- ## 4. Documentation update Add a brief "Interop" section to the top-level `Filament` moduledoc (in lib/filament.ex) mentioning `Filament.LiveComponent`: ``` ## Interop with existing LiveViews To embed a Filament component inside an existing Phoenix LiveView, use `Filament.LiveComponent`: <.live_component module={Filament.LiveComponent} id="cart" component={CartView} /> ``` --- ## 5. Acceptance criteria - [ ] `lib/filament/live_component.ex` exists and compiles - [ ] `Filament.LiveComponent` implements Phoenix.LiveComponent (mount/1, update/2, handle_event/3, render/1) - [ ] `update/2` correctly handles both first-mount (tree=nil) and re-render paths - [ ] `update/2` handles `filament_msg:` assign for observable forwarding - [ ] `handle_event/3` dispatches `filament:` events identically to Filament.LiveView - [ ] `@moduledoc` explains the observable forwarding requirement - [ ] `mix dialyzer` still passes after adding this module - [ ] `mix docs` still generates cleanly - [ ] `mix test` still passes (no regressions)
title: I5: LiveView interop adapter — Filament.LiveComponent (embed Filament in a regular LiveView)
